title: Bearings & Scale Drawings
description: Three-figure bearings, map scales, scale drawings and relating distances on a diagram to real distances.

notes.heading: What is a Bearing?

illustration.alt: Compass rose showing a bearing of 045 degrees measured clockwise from North.
illustration.caption: Bearings are measured clockwise from north and written with three figures.

notes.body:
📌 Definition
A bearing is an angle used to describe direction. Bearings are measured clockwise from north and are always written using three figures, such as $045^\circ$ or $270^\circ$.

🔑 Key Concept
To measure a bearing from point $A$ to point $B$:
1. Stand at point $A$ and face north.
2. Turn clockwise until you face point $B$.
3. The angle turned is the bearing of $B$ from $A$.

Because bearings use three figures, $5^\circ$ is written as $005^\circ$, and $90^\circ$ is written as $090^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example
What is the three-figure bearing for due east?

Step 1: Face north.

Step 2: Turn clockwise through $90^\circ$.

Step 3: Write as $090^\circ$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Bearings are always measured clockwise from north.
• Bearings are always written as three digits.
• North itself is $000^\circ$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Writing a bearing such as $45^\circ$ instead of $045^\circ$. Always include three figures, using leading zeros if necessary.

notes.heading: Compass Directions and Bearings
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Compass directions such as north (N), east (E), south (S) and west (W) describe the four main points of the compass. Bearings give a more precise clockwise angle from north.

🔑 Key Concept
The main compass bearings are:
• North: $000^\circ$
• East: $090^\circ$
• South: $180^\circ$
• West: $270^\circ$

Intermediate directions such as north-east lie halfway between two main points, so north-east is $045^\circ$ and south-east is $135^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example
Give the bearing for south-west.

Step 1: South-west is halfway between south ($180^\circ$) and west ($270^\circ$).

Step 2: Find the midpoint:
$$\dfrac{180^\circ + 270^\circ}{2} = 225^\circ$$

Step 3: Write the bearing as $225^\circ$.

✅ Check
South-west should be between $180^\circ$ and $270^\circ$. Since $225^\circ$ is exactly halfway, it is correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• North-east (NE) = $045^\circ$
• South-east (SE) = $135^\circ$
• South-west (SW) = $225^\circ$
• North-west (NW) = $315^\circ$

notes.heading: Map Scales as Ratios
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A map scale shows the relationship between a distance on a map and the corresponding real distance on the ground. Scales are often written as a ratio, such as $1 : 50\,000$.

🔑 How it works
The ratio $1 : 50\,000$ means that $1$ unit on the map represents $50\,000$ of the same units in real life. For example:
• $1$ cm on the map = $50\,000$ cm in real life
• $1$ cm on the map = $500$ m in real life
• $1$ cm on the map = $0.5$ km in real life

💡 Worked Example
A map has scale $1 : 25\,000$. How many metres does $1$ cm on the map represent?

Step 1: Interpret the ratio.
$$1 \text{ cm on map} = 25\,000 \text{ cm in real life}$$

Step 2: Convert centimetres to metres.
$$25\,000 \div 100 = 250 \text{ m}$$

So $1$ cm on the map represents $250$ m.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The first number in the ratio always refers to the map or drawing.
• Convert units carefully: $100$ cm = $1$ m and $1\,000$ m = $1$ km.
• The ratio itself has no units.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Forgetting to convert units. A scale of $1 : 100\,000$ means $1$ cm represents $1$ km, not $100\,000$ km.

notes.heading: Converting Map Distance to Real Distance
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To find a real distance from a map distance, multiply the map distance by the scale factor and then convert to sensible units.

🔑 How it works
If the scale is $1 : n$, then:
$$\text{real distance} = \text{map distance} \times n$$

Always make sure both distances are in the same units before comparing them.

💡 Worked Example
On a map with scale $1 : 50\,000$, two towns are $4$ cm apart. Find the real distance in kilometres.

Step 1: Multiply by the scale factor.
$$4 \times 50\,000 = 200\,000 \text{ cm}$$

Step 2: Convert centimetres to kilometres.
$$200\,000 \div 100 = 2\,000 \text{ m}$$
$$2\,000 \div 1\,000 = 2 \text{ km}$$

The real distance is $2$ km.

✅ Check
Use a rough estimate. Since $1$ cm = $0.5$ km, $4$ cm should be about $2$ km. The answer is sensible.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Map distance $\times$ scale factor = real distance in the same unit.
• Convert to metres or kilometres for final answers when appropriate.
• A larger scale factor means a smaller area is shown in more detail.

notes.heading: Scale Drawings
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A scale drawing is a diagram of a real object that is made larger or smaller by a fixed ratio, while keeping all angles and proportions the same.

🔑 Key Concept
A scale such as $1 : 10$ means the drawing is $10$ times smaller than the real object. A scale such as $10 : 1$ means the drawing is $10$ times larger than the real object.

If the scale is $1 : k$, then:
$$\text{drawing length} = \dfrac{\text{real length}}{k}$$

💡 Worked Example
A model car is made using a scale of $1 : 24$. The real car is $4.8$ m long. How long is the model in centimetres?

Step 1: Find the model length in metres.
$$4.8 \div 24 = 0.2 \text{ m}$$

Step 2: Convert to centimetres.
$$0.2 \times 100 = 20 \text{ cm}$$

The model is $20$ cm long.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• A scale drawing keeps the same shape but changes the size.
• The ratio tells you whether the drawing is smaller or larger than real life.
• Always check the order of numbers in the ratio.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Mixing up $1 : k$ and $k : 1$. If the object is smaller in the drawing, the first number must be smaller.

notes.heading: Bearings Combined with Distance
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Many problems combine bearings with distances. You may be asked to describe the position of one place relative to another using a bearing and a distance.

🔑 How it works
To describe point $B$ from point $A$:
1. Measure the bearing of $B$ from $A$ clockwise from north.
2. Measure or calculate the distance between $A$ and $B$.
3. State the answer as a bearing and a distance, for example: "$B$ is $12$ km from $A$ on a bearing of $060^\circ$."

💡 Worked Example
A ship sails $30$ km on a bearing of $090^\circ$ from port $P$ to point $Q$. Describe the return journey from $Q$ to $P$.

Step 1: Find the reverse bearing.
The return bearing is $180^\circ$ different from the outward bearing:
$$090^\circ + 180^\circ = 270^\circ$$

Step 2: State the distance.
The distance is the same, $30$ km.

Answer: The ship sails $30$ km on a bearing of $270^\circ$.

✅ Check
A bearing plus or minus $180^\circ$ points in the exact opposite direction. $270^\circ$ is due west, which is opposite due east ($090^\circ$).

📎 Key Points to Remember
• The reverse bearing is usually found by adding or subtracting $180^\circ$.
• If the original bearing is less than $180^\circ$, add $180^\circ$.
• If the original bearing is greater than $180^\circ$, subtract $180^\circ$.

notes.heading: Scale Drawings and Area
notes.body:
📌 Definition
When a shape is enlarged or reduced by a scale factor $k$, lengths are multiplied by $k$, but areas are multiplied by $k^2$. This is important when working with scale drawings of rooms, maps or models.

🔑 Key Concept
If a drawing uses scale $1 : k$, then:
$$\text{real length} = k \times \text{drawing length}$$
$$\text{real area} = k^2 \times \text{drawing area}$$

For example, with scale $1 : 100$, a length is $100$ times larger in real life, but an area is $100^2 = 10\,000$ times larger.

💡 Worked Example
A rectangular field is shown on a map with scale $1 : 5\,000$. On the map the field measures $2$ cm by $3$ cm. Find the real area in square metres.

Step 1: Find the real lengths.
$$2 \times 5\,000 = 10\,000 \text{ cm} = 100 \text{ m}$$
$$3 \times 5\,000 = 15\,000 \text{ cm} = 150 \text{ m}$$

Step 2: Find the real area.
$$100 \times 150 = 15\,000 \text{ m}^2$$

The real area is $15\,000$ m$^2$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Finding the area on the map and then multiplying by the scale factor instead of by the scale factor squared. Always square the scale factor when working with area.

✅ Check
Using the area formula directly gives the same result as squaring the scale factor.

flashcards.definition: An angle measured clockwise from north, written using three figures.
flashcards.example: $090^\circ$ is the bearing for due east.

flashcards.definition: A bearing always written with three digits, using leading zeros if necessary.
The bearing in the opposite direction, found by adding or subtracting $180^\circ$.
A ratio that compares a distance on a map to the corresponding real distance.
flashcards.example: $1 : 50\,000$ means $1$ cm on the map is $50\,000$ cm in real life.

flashcards.definition: The number in a scale ratio that tells you how many times larger or smaller the real object is.

flashcards.term: Converting map distance to real distance
flashcards.definition: Multiply the map distance by the scale factor, then convert to sensible units.
A diagram of a real object drawn larger or smaller by a fixed ratio while keeping the same shape.
flashcards.example: A $1 : 24$ model car is $\dfrac{1}{24}$ of the real car's length.

flashcards.definition: A scale where every unit on the drawing represents $k$ units in real life.
flashcards.example: $1 : 100$ means $1$ cm on the drawing is $100$ cm, or $1$ m, in real life.

flashcards.definition: When lengths are scaled by a factor $k$, areas are scaled by $k^2$.
flashcards.example: With scale $1 : 100$, an area is $100^2 = 10\,000$ times larger in real life.

flashcards.definition: A scale where the drawing is larger than the real object, used for very small objects.
flashcards.example: $10 : 1$ means the drawing is $10$ times larger than real life.

flashcards.definition: The clockwise angle measured at $A$, turning from north towards $B$.
flashcards.example: If $B$ is due south of $A$, the bearing of $B$ from $A$ is $180^\circ$.

questions.stem: Which of these is the correct three-figure bearing for due south?
questions.explanation: South is a half-turn clockwise from north, which is $180^\circ$. It is already three figures, so it is written as $180^\circ$.

questions.stem: What is $7^\circ$ written as a three-figure bearing?
questions.explanation: Three-figure bearings use leading zeros. Therefore $7^\circ$ is written as $007^\circ$.

questions.stem: What is the bearing for north-west?
questions.explanation: North-west is halfway between north ($000^\circ$) and west ($270^\circ$). The midpoint is $315^\circ$.

questions.stem: A map has scale $1 : 25\,000$. How many metres does $1$ cm on the map represent?
questions.explanation: $1$ cm represents $25\,000$ cm. Converting to metres gives $25\,000 \div 100 = 250$ m.

questions.stem: On a $1 : 50\,000$ map, two villages are $3$ cm apart. What is the real distance in kilometres?
A model is made with scale $1 : 20$. If the real object is $80$ cm long, how long is the model?
questions.explanation: With scale $1 : 20$, the model is $\dfrac{1}{20}$ of the real length. So $80 \div 20 = 4$ cm.

questions.stem: The bearing of point $B$ from point $A$ is $050^\circ$. What is the bearing of $A$ from $B$?
questions.explanation: The reverse bearing is found by adding $180^\circ$ because $050^\circ$ is less than $180^\circ$. So $050^\circ + 180^\circ = 230^\circ$.

questions.stem: What is the bearing for south-east?
questions.explanation: South-east is halfway between south ($180^\circ$) and east ($090^\circ$). The midpoint is $135^\circ$.

questions.stem: On a map, $2$ cm represents $1$ km. What is the scale written as a ratio?
questions.explanation: $1$ km = $100\,000$ cm. If $2$ cm represents $100\,000$ cm, then $1$ cm represents $50\,000$ cm, giving a scale of $1 : 50\,000$.

questions.stem: A scale drawing uses scale $1 : 100$. A room is $5$ m by $8$ m in real life. What are its dimensions on the drawing?
questions.explanation: With scale $1 : 100$, drawing lengths are $\dfrac{1}{100}$ of real lengths. So $5$ m = $500$ cm becomes $5$ cm, and $8$ m = $800$ cm becomes $8$ cm.

questions.stem: A field is drawn as a rectangle $2$ cm by $4$ cm using scale $1 : 5\,000$. What is the real area in square metres?
questions.explanation: Real lengths are $2 \times 5\,000 = 10\,000$ cm = $100$ m and $4 \times 5\,000 = 20\,000$ cm = $200$ m. The real area is $100 \times 200 = 20\,000$ m$^2$.

questions.stem: The bearing of $P$ from $Q$ is $210^\circ$. What is the bearing of $Q$ from $P$?
questions.explanation: The original bearing is greater than $180^\circ$, so subtract $180^\circ$. Thus $210^\circ - 180^\circ = 030^\circ$.

questions.stem: A map has scale $1 : 100\,000$. How many kilometres does $1$ cm represent?
questions.explanation: $1$ cm represents $100\,000$ cm. Since $100\,000$ cm = $1$ km, the answer is $1$ km.

questions.stem: A ship sails on a bearing of $120^\circ$. In which compass direction is it heading most closely?
questions.explanation: $120^\circ$ is between east ($090^\circ$) and south ($180^\circ$), so the ship is heading south-east.

questions.stem: A plan uses scale $1 : 200$. A garden measures $10$ m by $20$ m in real life. What is its area on the plan?
questions.explanation: Real dimensions convert to $10$ m = $1\,000$ cm $\rightarrow 1\,000 \div 200 = 5$ cm, and $20$ m = $2\,000$ cm $\rightarrow 2\,000 \div 200 = 10$ cm. The plan area is $5 \times 10 = 50$ cm$^2$.
